For most people, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best pick for the pool or beach.

## Top picks

- **Best overall: JBL Charge 6** (about $130-$150). It has an IP68 rating, so it's dust-sealed and survives submersion. Battery life is about 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost), and it can charge your phone. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and BestProducts did too. Buy links are on the [What Hi-Fi list](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) and the [BestProducts list](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).
- **Best for pool parties: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS rated it the best waterproof speaker it tested. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts 40+ hours. It's big and pricey, and the sound is muffled if you're behind or beside it. See the [RTINGS review](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth).
- **Best 360° sound: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** It's IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any seat. Battery life is about 15 hours. Tom's Guide picked it as best overall, and RTINGS named it best mid-range. See [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers) and [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth).
- **Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** (about $65-$80). It's softball-sized, IP67, floats, and gets about 14 hours of battery. It's quieter and has less bass than the bigger models. See [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/).
- **Best compact: JBL Grip** (about $100). It's can-shaped, under a pound, and IP68, with good sound for its size and 12 hours of battery. The mesh body collects sand and dust. See [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/).
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5** (about $40). It's IP67, but it's tiny and only gets 8-10 hours of battery. See [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart).

## What to look for

- **IP rating:** Aim for IP67 or higher for pool use. Good Housekeeping suggests at least IPX7, with IPX8 ideal ([source](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)).
- **Floating:** Pick a speaker that floats if it might get knocked in the pool.
- **Care:** IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use if the manufacturer allows it, keep the port covers closed, and let it dry fully before charging ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)).
